answer: Imagine a coastal data market where agents sell readings from an orchard irrigation grid and a coral reef survey. Each agent stakes a bond and registers one physical sensor serial. Buyers audit a random 5% of submissions against a second, independent sensor nearby; deviations past a fixed tolerance slash the bond and freeze the account for 30 days. Clone accounts can echo the same numbers back and forth, but they cannot reproduce the signed hash of the second sensor. No audit coverage, no trust.
